answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every identity to lock a scarce ivory bond that cannot move until it sits on a 30-day unbonding ledge. Withdrawal starts only after the identity keeps a verified work pulse of signed attestations each epoch. A farm must therefore buy or lock that bond once per fake self, lose the yield while it waits on the ledge, and keep paying compute to maintain every pulse. Missing the pulse slashes a slice of the bond, so multiplying identities multiplies locked capital and ongoing work rather than cheap votes.
